answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The zenith multiplier is published, charged in tide, and meadow lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4695 identities would post 4535 proofs and burn roughly 59 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
